# Psychoacoustic Metrics Index

> An index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics (loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness and psychoacoustic annoyance), organised by the standard edition or model each implementation follows. All programming languages.

Data as of 2026-10-06. 22 methods, 6 projects, languages: C, MATLAB, Python. Each implementation is tied to the standard edition or model paper it follows, with its validation evidence as stated by the project. Repository and package metadata are refreshed weekly.

## Loudness

- [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.md): current edition ISO 532-1:2017; implementations: MetaSona, MoSQITo, phonometry, pySQAT, SQAT
- [Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.md): current edition ISO 532-2:2017; implementations: phonometry
- [Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.md): current edition ISO 532-3:2023; implementations: phonometry
- [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: MetaSona, phonometry, pySQAT, sottek-hearing-model, SQAT

## Sharpness

- [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.md): current edition DIN 45692:2009; implementations: MetaSona, MoSQITo, phonometry, pySQAT, SQAT

## Roughness

- [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.md): current edition Daniel & Weber (1997); implementations: MetaSona, MoSQITo, pySQAT, SQAT
- [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: MetaSona, phonometry, pySQAT, sottek-hearing-model, SQAT
- [Roughness, DIN 38455](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-din-38455.md): current edition DIN 38455:2024; implementations: none found

## Fluctuation strength

- [Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.md): current edition Osses et al. (2016); implementations: phonometry, pySQAT, SQAT
- [Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: phonometry, sottek-hearing-model, SQAT

## Tonality

- [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.md): current edition Aures (1985b); implementations: MetaSona, pySQAT, SQAT, MoSQITo
- [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: MetaSona, phonometry, pySQAT, sottek-hearing-model, SQAT
- [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.md): current edition ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.); implementations: phonometry
- [Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-din-45681.md): current edition DIN 45681:2005; implementations: none found
- [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.md): current edition ISO/TS 20065:2022; implementations: none found
- [Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.md): current edition ISO 1996-2:2017; implementations: phonometry, MoSQITo
- [Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.md): current edition IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018; implementations: phonometry

## Impulsiveness

- [Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/impulsiveness.md): current edition ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022; implementations: phonometry

## Psychoacoustic annoyance

- [Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.md): current edition Widmann (1992), Zwicker & Fastl (1999), More (2010), and Di et al. (2016); implementations: pySQAT, SQAT, phonometry

## Related quantities

- [Equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.md): current edition ISO 226:2023; implementations: phonometry
- [Perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/epnl.md): current edition ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I and 14 CFR Part 36; implementations: pySQAT, SQAT, phonometry
- [Aural detectability of sounds in background noise](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/aural-detectability.md): current edition Fidell et al. (1974); implementations: none found

## Projects

- [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.md): Python, C; C library with a typed Python interface and prebuilt wheels, written to make repeated psychoacoustic analysis fast.
- [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.md): Python; Python library for sound quality metrics: ISO 532-1 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness, ECMA-418-2 loudness and roughness (2nd edition), tone-to-noise and prominence ratios, and the speech intelligibility index.
- [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.md): Python; Python acoustics library (formerly PyOctaveBand) that added a large psychoacoustics module in July 2026: ISO 532-1, -2 and -3 loudness, ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness, tonality, roughness and fluctuation strength (monaural), DIN 45692 sharpness, Osses fluctuation strength, ECMA-418-1:2024 TNR/PR, tonal audibility, impulsiveness, EPNL and ISO 226:2023.
- [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.md): Python; Python port of the MATLAB toolbox SQAT (README title "SQAT4PY") with a PySide6 graphical interface.
- [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.md): Python; Python implementation of the ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th edition) Sottek Hearing Model metrics: loudness, tonality and roughness, with binaural combination, and fluctuation strength on the main branch.
- [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.md): MATLAB; MATLAB toolbox for sound quality analysis that bundles most psychoacoustic metrics in one place: ISO 532-1 and ECMA-418-2 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber and ECMA-418-2 roughness, Osses fluctuation strength, Aures and ECMA-418-2 tonality, four psychoacoustic annoyance models and EPNL.

## Data

- [index.json](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/index.json): the complete index as JSON
- [llms-full.txt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/llms-full.txt): all pages in one Markdown file
- [Data schema](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/blob/main/data/SCHEMA.md)

# About this index

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/about.html

An index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics (loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness and psychoacoustic annoyance), organised by the standard edition or model each implementation follows. All programming languages.

## What is included

Open-source code that computes a psychoacoustic metric and says which model or standard edition it follows. Quantities: loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness, psychoacoustic annoyance, and related quantities. Not included: LUFS / ITU-R BS.1770, speech intelligibility, codec quality metrics (PEAQ, PESQ, ViSQOL), psychophysics experiment software and closed-source tools. Reference programs that are free to download but not open source (such as the ISO 532 programs) are listed and marked.

## How entries are checked

Each entry is written from the project's own README, documentation, release notes, licence file and package metadata, with links to those sources. The index records what a project claims; it does not run the code. Repository dates, releases and package versions are refreshed every week by a GitHub Action, which also searches for new candidate projects and watches the standards bodies for new editions. A person reviews the findings before anything is added.

## Status of an implementation

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| available | In the latest release, or on the default branch of a project without releases. |
| unreleased | Merged on the default branch but newer than the latest release. |
| proposed | Open pull request or separate branch, not merged. |

## Validation evidence

As stated by each project:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| standard or paper data | Compared with test signals or values published in the standard or the model paper. |
| reference code | Compared with the reference program or the model authors' own code. |
| another implementation | Compared with another independent implementation. |
| own tests only | Tests exist, but without external reference data. |
| not stated | The project does not say how it was validated. |

## Leads not yet verified

Candidates that may belong in the index but could not be checked yet; nothing here has been confirmed.

- [PsyTools (TU Graz)](https://gitlab.tugraz.at/11F34386B3DC1474/psytools) (Python): Search results describe a Python toolbox with ISO 532-1 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, ECMA-418 tonality and hearing model, fluctuation strength, roughness and psychoacoustic annoyance (paper from May 2026). The GitLab host could not be reached from the checking environment.
- [ITA-Toolbox (RWTH Aachen)](https://git.rwth-aachen.de/ita/toolbox) (MATLAB): Contains `ita_loudness` and `ita_loudness_timevariant` (associated with ISO 532 in search results). The GitLab host could not be reached from the checking environment.
- [Genesis Loudness Toolbox](http://www.genesis-acoustics.com/index.php?page=32) (MATLAB): Free MATLAB toolbox (about 2010) said to cover ISO 532B, ANSI S3.4-2007, Glasberg & Moore (2002), Zwicker's time-varying model and a loudness model for impulsive sounds. The download page could not be reached; licence and availability are unknown.
- [Codes for the rapid calculation of loudness and sharpness (MATLAB File Exchange 73808)](https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/73808-codes-for-the-rapid-calculation-of-loudness-and-sharpness) (MATLAB): Sharpness computed from Moore–Glasberg (ANSI S3.4) specific loudness after Swift & Gee (2017), plus several loudness methods. MATLAB File Exchange could not be reached from the checking environment.
- [Salford sound quality MATLAB codes](https://acoustics.salford.ac.uk/psychoacoustics/sound-quality-making-products-sound-better/an-introduction-to-sound-quality-testing/matlab-codes/) (MATLAB): Functions named `loudness_1991`, `sharpness_Fastl` and `roughness4`. The page could not be reached; models and licence are unknown.
- [Time-varying specific loudness GUI (HAW Hamburg)](https://zenodo.org/records/7361480) (MATLAB): MATLAB interface for Chalupper & Fastl (2002), Baumgarte (2000) and Glasberg & Moore specific loudness. Zenodo could not be reached from the checking environment.
- [Mosqito.NET](https://github.com/onur-akaydin/Mosqito.NET) (C#): C# / .NET port of MoSQITo (Apache-2.0), announced in MoSQITo issue Not checked yet.
- [Cambridge Hearing Group loudness programs](https://www.psychol.cam.ac.uk/hearing#programs) (MATLAB): Programs for the Moore–Glasberg loudness models from the models' authors; LoudnessModel names this page as the source of the MATLAB code it translated. The page could not be reached; licence terms are unknown.

Not indexed because they are closed source: MATLAB Audio Toolbox, HEAD acoustics ArtemiS SUITE, Simcenter Testlab, HBK BK Connect and Ansys Sound.

## Machine-readable data

- [index.json](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/index.json): the whole index as JSON
- [llms.txt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/llms.txt) and [llms-full.txt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/llms-full.txt): summaries for language models
- [feed.xml](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/feed.xml): Atom feed of updates
- Source data and schema: https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/tree/main/data

## Contributing and citing

Corrections and new projects are welcome through issues or pull requests: https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index. To cite the index, use the CITATION.cff file in the repository. Maintained by Zhenxian Li. Licence: MIT.

# Frequently asked questions

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/faq.html

## Which psychoacoustic metrics can I compute in Python?

Current editions of 18 methods have an available implementation that can be called from Python: [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), [Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html), [Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html), [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), [Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html), [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html), [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html), [Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html), [Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.html), [Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/impulsiveness.html), [Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), [Equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html), and [Perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/epnl.html). Projects: MetaSona, MoSQITo, phonometry, pySQAT, sottek-hearing-model.

## Which psychoacoustic metrics can I compute in MATLAB/Octave?

Current editions of 7 methods have an available implementation that can be called from MATLAB/Octave: [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html), [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), [Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html), [Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html), and [Perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/epnl.html). Projects: SQAT.

## Which psychoacoustic metrics can I compute in C/C++?

Current editions of 7 methods have an available implementation that can be called from C/C++: [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html), [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html), and [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html). Projects: MetaSona.

## Which open-source code implements Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)?

The current edition is ISO 532-1:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-1. Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; stationary and time-varying), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; stationary and time-varying).

## Which open-source code implements Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)?

The current edition is ISO 532-2:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-2. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; with binaural inhibition).

## Which open-source code implements time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)?

The current edition is ISO 532-3:2023. In development: ISO/CD 532-3. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python).

## Which open-source code implements loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; mono only), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (Python; mono or stereo, with combined binaural output), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; unreleased). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.); mono or two channels with binaural combination) and [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)).

## Which open-source code implements sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)?

The current edition is DIN 45692:2009. Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; from specific loudness), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; also the informative Aures and von Bismarck variants), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; DIN 45692 weighting, plus von Bismarck and Aures options).

## Which open-source code implements roughness, Daniel & Weber model?

There is no standard; the reference model is Daniel & Weber (1997). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB).

## Which open-source code implements roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; mono only; no entropy weighting), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (Python; with combined binaural output), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; unreleased). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.); with binaural combination) and [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)).

## Which open-source code implements roughness, DIN 38455?

The current edition is DIN 38455:2024. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which open-source code implements fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula?

There is no standard; the reference model is Osses et al. (2016). Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; Fastl & Zwicker (2007); closed-form expression for amplitude-modulated noise).

## Which open-source code implements fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; mono only), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (Python; needs at least 1.37 s of signal; binaural option; unreleased), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; proposed, not merged).

## Which open-source code implements tonality, Aures/Terhardt model?

There is no standard; the reference model is Aures (1985b). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB), and [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; proposed, not merged).

## Which open-source code implements tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; mono or stereo), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; mono only), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; unreleased). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)).

## Which open-source code implements tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)).

## Which open-source code implements tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)?

The current edition is DIN 45681:2005. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which open-source code implements audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)?

The current edition is ISO/TS 20065:2022. No open-source implementation of it has been found. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; ISO/PAS 20065:2016).

## Which open-source code implements tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)?

The current edition is ISO 1996-2:2017. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; Annex K survey method and Table J.1; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) and [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; Annex K prominent-tone detection; proposed, not merged). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; ISO 1996-2:2007; Annex C; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace).

## Which open-source code implements tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)?

The current edition is IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python).

## Which open-source code implements prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)?

The current edition is ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; NT ACOU 112; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace).

## Which open-source code implements psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)?

There is no standard; the reference models are Widmann (1992), Zwicker & Fastl (1999), More (2010), and Di et al. (2016). In development: ISO/AWI 26573. Open-source implementations of it: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; Di et al. (2016)), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; Di et al. (2016)), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; More (2010)), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; More (2010)), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; Widmann (1992); unreleased).

## Which open-source code implements equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)?

The current edition is ISO 226:2023. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; ISO 226:2003).

## Which open-source code implements perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)?

The current edition is ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I and 14 CFR Part 36. Open-source implementations of it: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; 14 CFR Part 36), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; 14 CFR Part 36), and [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I; PNL, PNLT and EPNL, in the `phonometry.aircraft` namespace).

## Which open-source code implements aural detectability of sounds in background noise?

There is no standard; the reference model is Fidell et al. (1974). No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which psychoacoustic metrics have no open-source implementation yet?

No available open-source implementation of the current edition was found for [Roughness, DIN 38455](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-din-38455.html), [Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html), [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html), and [Aural detectability of sounds in background noise](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/aural-detectability.html).

## Why does it matter which edition a tool implements?

Psychoacoustic standards change between editions. ECMA-418-2, for example, has had four editions since 2020 that changed the hearing model, roughness and loudness, and all three parts of ISO 532 are being revised. Two tools that both claim to implement a standard can therefore give different values for the same sound. Each method page lists the editions and which tool follows which.

## How are the entries checked?

From each project's own README, documentation, release notes, licence file and package metadata, with links to those sources. The index records what a project claims and does not run the code. Repository and package metadata are refreshed every week, and a person reviews new findings.


---

# Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-1, ISO 532B, ISO 532 method B, DIN 45631, DIN 45631/A1, Zwicker method, N5, percentile loudness

Loudness from Zwicker's model: third-octave band levels are turned into specific loudness on the critical-band (Bark) scale and integrated. ISO 532-1:2017 specifies one procedure for stationary sounds and one for time-varying sounds (from which percentile values such as N5 are taken), and replaced method B of ISO 532:1975. The German standards DIN 45631 (stationary) and DIN 45631/A1 (time-varying) describe the same method.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO 532-1:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-1. Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; stationary and time-varying), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; stationary and time-varying).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-1](https://www.iso.org/standard/90809.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2017-06 | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Stationary and time-varying procedures; Annex A reference program, Annex B test signals. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 2010-03 | [DIN 45631/A1:2010](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631-a1/122476084) | current | Adds the procedure for time-varying sounds. | — |
| 2002 | Chalupper & Fastl (2002) | published | Dynamic loudness model built on Zwicker's model, also for hearing impairment (not standardised). | — |
| 1991-03 | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) | current | Stationary sounds. | — |
| 1975-07 | [ISO 532:1975](https://www.iso.org/standard/4603.html) | withdrawn | Method B (Zwicker) for stationary sounds, from third-octave levels. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels; since 0.1.0) | `stationary_loudness`, `time_varying_loudness`, `loudness_from_levels` | another implementation | Model tables taken from MoSQITo and checked element by element; one upper-slope value (0.22) follows the ISO 532-1 reference C table where MoSQITo uses 0.24. |
| [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) | Python | ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying; since 1.0.0) | `loudness_zwst`, `loudness_zwst_perseg`, `loudness_zwst_freq`, `loudness_zwtv` | standard or paper data | Validation scripts use the ISO 532-1 Annex B test signals; the documentation marks it as validated. |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary and time-varying; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_zwicker`, `loudness_zwicker_from_spectrum` | standard or paper data | Written from the Annex A reference program; Annex B test signals are used in the tests. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | ISO 532-1:2017 | `Loudness_ISO532_1` | another implementation | Compared with SQAT (MATLAB). |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary and time-varying; since v1.0) | `Loudness_ISO532_1`, `Loudness_ISO532_1_from_wavfile` | standard or paper data | Checked with the 25 test signals of Annex B.2–B.5 against the standard's tolerances. Fixes to the time-varying procedure are on `main` only (PR #48). |

**See also:** [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

# Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4, ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007, Moore-Glasberg method, Cambridge loudness model

Loudness of stationary sounds from the Moore–Glasberg model: the spectrum is turned into an excitation pattern on the ERB-number scale, then into specific loudness, which is summed. ANSI S3.4-2007 standardised the model of Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) with later modifications; ISO 532-2:2017 specifies the method for monaural and binaural listening.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO 532-2:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-2. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; with binaural inhibition).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-2](https://www.iso.org/standard/90812.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2017-06 | [ISO 532-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63078.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Monaural and binaural loudness of stationary sounds; source code supplied with the standard. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2011 | [Chen et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001) | published | Faster excitation-pattern calculation, also for hearing loss (not standardised). | — |
| 2007 | [ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007](https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020) | current | American standard based on the 1997 model with later modifications. | — |
| 1997 | Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) | published | Model paper (thresholds, loudness and partial loudness). | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ISO 532-2:2017 (with binaural inhibition; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_moore_glasberg`, `loudness_moore_glasberg_from_spectrum`, `loudness_moore_glasberg_from_third_octave` | standard or paper data | The documentation says it reproduces the Annex B tone and broadband cases to within a percent or two. |

**See also:** [Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html)

## References

1. Moore, B. C. J., Glasberg, B. R., & Baer, T. (1997). A model for the prediction of thresholds, loudness, and partial loudness. *Journal of the Audio Engineering Society*, 45(4), 224–240.
2. ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007. Procedure for the Computation of Loudness of Steady Sounds. https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020
3. Chen, Z., Hu, G., Glasberg, B. R., & Moore, B. C. J. (2011). A new method of calculating auditory excitation patterns and loudness for steady sounds. *Hearing Research*, 282(1–2), 204–215. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001
4. ISO 532-2:2017. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 2: Moore-Glasberg method. https://www.iso.org/standard/63078.html
5. ISO/CD 532-2. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 2: Moore-Glasberg method (2nd edition). https://www.iso.org/standard/90812.html

# Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-3, TVL, time-varying loudness, Glasberg and Moore 2002, Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method, short-term loudness, long-term loudness

Loudness of time-varying sounds as instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness. It starts from the Glasberg & Moore (2002) model; Moore et al. (2016) added binaural inhibition and Moore et al. (2018) revised the time constants. ISO 532-3:2023 standardises the resulting Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher method for stationary and time-varying sounds.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO 532-3:2023. In development: ISO/CD 532-3. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-3](https://www.iso.org/standard/90816.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2023-07 | [ISO 532-3:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Standardised method; source code supplied with the standard. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2018 | [Moore et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246) | published | Revised time constants. | — |
| 2016 | [Moore et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698) | published | Adds binaural inhibition. | — |
| 2002 | Glasberg & Moore (2002) | published | Time-varying loudness model (short-term and long-term loudness). | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ISO 532-3:2023 (since 3.1.0) | `loudness_moore_glasberg_time` | standard or paper data | Documented deviations: it runs at the native sample rate instead of resampling to 32 kHz, and the Annex B WAV-file cases are not reproduced (Annex C values are used instead). |

**See also:** [Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html)

## References

1. Glasberg, B. R., & Moore, B. C. J. (2002). A model of loudness applicable to time-varying sounds. *Journal of the Audio Engineering Society*, 50(5), 331–342.
2. Moore, B. C. J., Glasberg, B. R., Varathanathan, A., & Schlittenlacher, J. (2016). A loudness model for time-varying sounds incorporating binaural inhibition. *Trends in Hearing*, 20, 2331216516682698. https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698
3. Moore, B. C. J., Jervis, M., Harries, L., & Schlittenlacher, J. (2018). Testing and refining a loudness model for time-varying sounds incorporating binaural inhibition. *The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America*, 143(3), 1504–1513. https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246
4. ISO 532-3:2023. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 3: Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method. https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html
5. ISO/CD 532-3. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 3: Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method (2nd edition). https://www.iso.org/standard/90816.html

# Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 loudness, Sottek Hearing Model, SHM loudness, sone_HMS, hearing model loudness

Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model defined in ECMA-418-2. The hearing model (Clause 5) produces specific loudness; the 2nd edition (2022) added a loudness calculation for sounds with tonal and noise components (Clause 8). ECMA-418-2 has had four editions in five years, so implementations of different editions can disagree.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; mono only), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (Python; mono or stereo, with combined binaural output), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; unreleased). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.); mono or two channels with binaural combination) and [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | Hearing-model clauses 5.1.2.2 and 5.1.5.2 revised; conformance requires 48 kHz sampling. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (unreleased) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Adds a diffuse-field outer and middle ear filter. | [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | New Clause 8, loudness of sounds with subcritical or wider bandwidth. | [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Hearing model (Clause 5) with specific loudness. | — |

# Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html

**Quantity:** Sharpness · **Unit:** acum · **Also known as:** DIN 45692, acum, Zwicker sharpness, Aures sharpness, von Bismarck sharpness

Sharpness is the weighted first moment of specific loudness along the critical-band rate, with a weighting that emphasises high frequencies. DIN 45692:2009 standardises the weighting and a test procedure, using Zwicker specific loudness (ISO 532-1 / DIN 45631). Most implementations also offer the weightings of von Bismarck (1974) and Aures (1985).

**In short.** The current edition is DIN 45692:2009. Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; from specific loudness), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; also the informative Aures and von Bismarck variants), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; DIN 45692 weighting, plus von Bismarck and Aures options).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2009-08 | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) | current | Standardised weighting and test procedure; no revision announced. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 2007 | [Fastl & Zwicker (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4) | published | Zwicker & Fastl weighting as given in the textbook. | — |
| 1985 | Aures (1985b) | published | Weighting that depends on total loudness. | — |
| 1974 | von Bismarck (1974) | published | Original sharpness weighting. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | DIN 45692:2009 (from specific loudness; since 0.1.0) | `sharpness_din45692` | not stated | — |
| [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) | Python | DIN 45692:2009 (weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl; since 1.0.2) | `sharpness_din_st`, `sharpness_din_tv`, `sharpness_din_perseg`, `sharpness_din_from_loudness`, `sharpness_din_freq` | standard or paper data | Validation scripts use the DIN 45692 test signals; the documentation marks it as validated. |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | DIN 45692:2009 (also the informative Aures and von Bismarck variants; since 3.1.0) | `sharpness_din`, `sharpness_din_from_specific` | standard or paper data | Checked with the DIN 45692 reference signal and Table A.2. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | DIN 45692:2009 | `Sharpness_DIN45692`, `Sharpness_DIN45692_from_loudness` | another implementation | Compared with SQAT (MATLAB). |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | DIN 45692:2009 (DIN 45692 weighting, plus von Bismarck and Aures options; since v1.0) | `Sharpness_DIN45692`, `Sharpness_DIN45692_from_loudness`, `Sharpness_DIN45692_from_wavfile` | standard or paper data | Checked with the narrowband and broadband test signals of DIN 45692. |

**See also:** [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html)

## References

1. von Bismarck, G. (1974). Sharpness as an attribute of the timbre of steady sounds. *Acustica*, 30(3), 159–172.
2. Aures, W. (1985). Berechnungsverfahren für den sensorischen Wohlklang beliebiger Schallsignale [A model for calculating the sensory euphony of various sounds]. *Acustica*, 59, 130–141.

# Roughness, Daniel & Weber model

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper · **Also known as:** Daniel and Weber roughness, Daniel & Weber 1997, Aures roughness, asper

Roughness from the model of Daniel & Weber (1997), an optimised version of Aures's (1985) model. It is not standardised, and the paper leaves details open (filter bank, calibration, framing), so implementations can give different values for the same signal.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference model is Daniel & Weber (1997). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB).

SQAT replaced its implementation in September 2026 with one that follows Dik Hermes's code, which changes results compared with SQAT v1.3 and earlier.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1997 | Daniel & Weber (1997) | published | Reference model. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 1985 | Aures (1985a) | published | Earlier model that Daniel & Weber optimised. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | Daniel & Weber (1997) (since 0.1.0) | `roughness_daniel_weber` | another implementation | Follows SQAT revision `e6228b78`, which includes SQAT's September 2026 rewrite. |
| [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) | Python | Daniel & Weber (1997) (since 1.0.0) | `roughness_dw`, `roughness_dw_freq` | standard or paper data | The documentation marks it as validated against reference data. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | Daniel & Weber (1997) | `Roughness_Daniel1997` | another implementation | Compared with SQAT v1.3, before SQAT's September 2026 rewrite. |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | Daniel & Weber (1997) (since v1.0) | `Roughness_Daniel1997`, `Roughness_Daniel1997_from_wavfile` | standard or paper data | Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature. Rewritten on `main` (PR #65, 2026-09-08) after revised code from Dik Hermes: 63 of 119 validation values go up and 56 down (largest change 0.155 asper). |

**See also:** [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

1. Aures, W. (1985). Ein Berechnungsverfahren der Rauhigkeit [A procedure for calculating auditory roughness]. *Acustica*, 58, 268–281.
2. Daniel, P., & Weber, R. (1997). Psychoacoustical roughness: Implementation of an optimized model. *Acta Acustica united with Acustica*, 83(1), 113–123.

# Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 roughness, asper_HMS, Sottek roughness, SHM roughness

Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model, Clause 7 of ECMA-418-2. The 2nd edition (2022) added an optional entropy weighting for cases where rotational speed is measured; the 3rd edition (2024) changed zero-padding and segmentation, the largest change to roughness so far.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; mono only; no entropy weighting), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (Python; with combined binaural output), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; unreleased). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.); with binaural combination) and [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | Hearing-model and conformance updates (48 kHz sampling). | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (unreleased) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Zero-padding and segmentation adapted; main revision of roughness. | [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Refined calculation; optional entropy-weighted roughness. | [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Clause 7 roughness. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied; since 0.2.0) | `roughness_ecma` | another implementation | Uses the standard's 20 ms grid and nominal calibration factor, where SQAT uses a slightly adjusted calibration. |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono only; no entropy weighting; since 3.1.0) | `roughness_ecma` | standard or paper data | Checked at the calibration signal only. |

| [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) | Python | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (with combined binaural output; since 0.1.9) | `shm_roughness_ecma` | standard or paper data | — |

# Roughness, DIN 38455

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-din-38455.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper · **Also known as:** DIN 38455, Rauigkeit, German roughness standard

DIN 38455:2024 is the first German standard for calculating roughness. Its text is not freely available, and the model it specifies could not be confirmed from public sources; a hearing-model roughness was proposed for DIN standardisation by Sottek & Becker (2019).

**In short.** The current edition is DIN 38455:2024. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [DIN 38455:2024](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-38455/376186532) | current | First edition. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html)

## References

1. DIN 38455:2024. Berechnung der Hörempfindung Rauigkeit (Calculation of the auditory sensation of roughness). https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-38455/376186532


---

# Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html

**Quantity:** Fluctuation strength · **Unit:** vacil · **Also known as:** fluctuation strength, vacil, Osses 2016, Fastl and Zwicker fluctuation strength

Fluctuation strength describes slow modulation around 4 Hz. Osses, García & Kohlrausch (2016) proposed a signal-based model; Fastl & Zwicker give a closed-form expression for modulated tones and noises. Neither is standardised. ECMA-418-2:2025 added a hearing-model method, listed on its own page.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference model is Osses et al. (2016). Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; Fastl & Zwicker (2007); closed-form expression for amplitude-modulated noise).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | [Osses et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410) | published | Signal-based model. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 2007 | [Fastl & Zwicker (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4) | published | Closed-form expression for amplitude- and frequency-modulated sounds. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | Osses et al. (2016) (since 3.1.0) | `fluctuation_strength` | standard or paper data | Compared with Table 1 of Osses et al. (2016) and with SQAT (correlation 0.98). Validated for amplitude modulation only; a steady 1 kHz tone reads about 0.09 vacil. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | Osses et al. (2016) | `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016` | another implementation | — |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | Osses et al. (2016) (since v1.0) | `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016`, `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016_from_wavfile` | standard or paper data | Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature. |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | Fastl & Zwicker (2007) (closed-form expression for amplitude-modulated noise; since 3.1.0) | `fluctuation_strength_am_noise` | not stated | — |

**See also:** [Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

1. Fastl, H., & Zwicker, E. (2007). *Psychoacoustics: Facts and models* (3rd ed.). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4
2. Osses Vecchi, A., García León, R., & Kohlrausch, A. (2016). Modelling the sensation of fluctuation strength. *Proceedings of Meetings on Acoustics*, 28, 050005. https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410

# Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Fluctuation strength · **Unit:** vacil_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 fluctuation strength, vacil_HMS, Sottek fluctuation strength

Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model, new in the 4th edition of ECMA-418-2 (June 2025, Clause 9). It uses high-resolution spectral analysis for modulation rates of about 0.25 to 20 Hz.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; mono only), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (Python; needs at least 1.37 s of signal; binaural option; unreleased), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; proposed, not merged).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | New Clause 9. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (unreleased), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (proposed) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono only; since 3.3.0) | `fluctuation_strength_ecma` | standard or paper data | Checked at the calibration signal only (0.993 vacil_HMS); misprints found in Clause 9 are listed in its errata. |
| [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) | Python | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (needs at least 1.37 s of signal; binaural option) | `shm_fluctuation_ecma` | another implementation | Unreleased. Merged on 2026-09-18. A draft report compares it with the MATLAB version (equal to floating-point precision) and with HEAD ArtemiS SUITE v17 (calibration 0.994 vs 1.003 vacil_HMS; recordings −8 % to +12 %). Five departures from the printed equations, judged to be misprints, are documented. |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) | `FluctuationStrength_ECMA418_2` | not stated | Proposed (https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/78). Open pull request since 2026-09-17. |

**See also:** [Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

# Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** t.u. · **Also known as:** Aures tonality, Terhardt tonality, tonality units, t.u., sensory euphony

Tonality from Aures (1985): tonal components are extracted with the method of Terhardt, Stoll & Seewann (1982), weighted, and related to the loudness of the whole sound. Not standardised.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference model is Aures (1985b). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB), and [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; proposed, not merged).

SQAT corrected several issues in September 2026 (for example, only the first tonal component entered the weighting), which changes results compared with SQAT v1.3 and earlier.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | Aures (1985b) | published | Tonality model. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (proposed) |
| 1982 | [Terhardt et al. (1982)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.387544) | published | Extraction of tonal components used by the model. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | Aures (1985b) (since 0.1.0) | `tonality_aures` | another implementation | Follows SQAT's September 2026 revision (250 ms Hann windows, 125 ms hop); exact agreement with MATLAB is not established. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | Aures (1985b) | `Tonality_Aures1985` | another implementation | A June 2026 commit corrected its calibration; it predates SQAT's September 2026 fixes. |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | Aures (1985b) (since v1.0) | `Tonality_Aures1985`, `Tonality_Aures1985_from_wavfile` | standard or paper data | v1.3 is checked with one signal-to-noise comparison. Eight defects were fixed on `main` in September 2026 (for example, only one tonal component's level excess entered the result, and tones were removed from the wrong spectrum), with new checks against Aures's Figs. 5 and 6. |
| [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) | Python | Aures (1985b) | — | not stated | Proposed (https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/97). Pull request from April 2026 following the improved Aures metric of Estreder et al. (2023); no maintainer reply. |

**See also:** [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

1. Terhardt, E., Stoll, G., & Seewann, M. (1982). Algorithm for extraction of pitch and pitch salience from complex tonal signals. *The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America*, 71(3), 679–688. https://doi.org/10.1121/1.387544
2. Aures, W. (1985). Berechnungsverfahren für den sensorischen Wohlklang beliebiger Schallsignale [A model for calculating the sensory euphony of various sounds]. *Acustica*, 59, 130–141.
