# Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** tu_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 tonality, psychoacoustic tonality, tu_HMS, Sottek tonality, SHM tonality

Psychoacoustic tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model, Clause 6 of ECMA-418-2, with specific tonality and tonal frequency over time. The method came from ECMA-74 (17th edition, 2019) when ECMA-418-2 was first published in 2020.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; mono or stereo), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; mono only), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html) (Python), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; unreleased). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | Hearing-model and conformance updates (48 kHz sampling). | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [sottek-hearing-model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (unreleased) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Further refinement. | [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Refined calculation. | — |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Clause 6 tonality. | — |
| 2019-12 | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) | superseded | Hearing model and tonality before ECMA-418-2 existed. | — |

# Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** TNR, PR, ECMA-418-1, ECMA-74 Annex D, prominent discrete tones, ANSI S1.13 Annex

Tone-to-noise ratio (TNR) and prominence ratio (PR) decide whether a discrete tone is prominent: TNR compares the tone with the noise in its critical band, PR compares the critical band with its neighbours. ECMA-418-1 took the method over from Annex D of ECMA-74 in 2020; its 3rd edition (2024) revised the TNR procedure.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | current | TNR procedure revised for repeatable results across FFT resolutions; terms rewritten. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Maximum tone bandwidth for TNR set to 15 % of the critical band; corrections. | — |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Based on, and mostly identical to, ECMA-74 Annex D. | — |
| 2019-12 | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) | superseded | Annex D, before ECMA-418-1 existed. | [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.) (since 3.1.0) | `tone_to_noise_ratio`, `prominence_ratio`, `assess_tones` | standard or paper data | The "prominent" flag applies the numeric criterion only. |
| [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) | Python | ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.) (since 1.0.2) | `tnr_ecma_st`, `tnr_ecma_perseg`, `tnr_ecma_freq`, `pr_ecma_st`, `pr_ecma_perseg`, `pr_ecma_freq` | not stated | Docstrings say "ECMA 418-1" without an edition; the helper code and the bibliography cite ECMA-74 Annex D (17th edition, 2019). The documentation marks it as available but not validated. |

**See also:** [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html)

## References

1. ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.). Measurement of airborne noise emitted by information technology and telecommunications equipment. https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/
2. ECMA-418-1:2020 (1st ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 1 (prominent discrete tones). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf
3. ECMA-418-1:2022 (2nd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 1 (prominent discrete tones). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf
4. ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 1 (prominent discrete tones). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf

# Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** DIN 45681, tone adjustment, K_T, Tonzuschlag

German method that detects tonal components in noise from narrow-band spectra and derives a tone adjustment for the assessment of noise immissions. DIN 45681:2005 with its corrections of 2005 and 2006 is current.

**In short.** The current edition is DIN 45681:2005. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2005-03 | [DIN 45681:2005](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45681/76463232) | current | Current, with corrections of 2005-08 and 2006-08. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html)

## References

1. DIN 45681:2005. Akustik — Bestimmung der Tonhaltigkeit von Geräuschen und Ermittlung eines Tonzuschlages für die Beurteilung von Geräuschimmissionen. https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45681/76463232

# Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** ISO/TS 20065, ISO/PAS 20065, tonal audibility, decisive audibility, ΔL_ta

Engineering method for the audibility of tones in noise, from critical-band analysis of narrow-band spectra. First published as ISO/PAS 20065:2016 and turned into ISO/TS 20065:2022, which notes that the method is not validated below 50 Hz.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO/TS 20065:2022. No open-source implementation of it has been found. Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; ISO/PAS 20065:2016).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022-12 | [ISO/TS 20065:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/81518.html) | current | Technical specification; adds that the method is not validated below 50 Hz. | — |
| 2016-07 | [ISO/PAS 20065:2016](https://www.iso.org/standard/66941.html) | withdrawn | Publicly available specification; withdrawn in 2022. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ISO/PAS 20065:2016 (since 3.1.0) | `tone_audibility`, `analyze_spectrum`, `audibility_from_levels`, `mean_audibility`, `audibility_uncertainty` | standard or paper data | Follows the 2016 PAS, not the 2022 TS. Does not apply the A-weighting required by clause 5.3.2. |

**See also:** [Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html), [Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html)

## References

1. ISO/PAS 20065:2016. Acoustics — Objective method for assessing the audibility of tones in noise — Engineering method. https://www.iso.org/standard/66941.html
2. ISO/TS 20065:2022. Acoustics — Objective method for assessing the audibility of tones in noise — Engineering method. https://www.iso.org/standard/81518.html

# Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** ISO 1996-2 Annex C, ISO 1996-2 Annex J, ISO 1996-2 Annex K, tonal adjustment, environmental noise tonality

Objective tonal audibility and tone adjustment for environmental noise assessment. ISO 1996-2:2007 gave a method in Annex C; ISO 1996-2:2017 replaced it with an engineering method (Annex J) and a survey method (Annex K).

**In short.** The current edition is ISO 1996-2:2017. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; Annex K survey method and Table J.1; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) and [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; Annex K prominent-tone detection; proposed, not merged). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; ISO 1996-2:2007; Annex C; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2017-07 | [ISO 1996-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/59766.html) | current | Annex J engineering method and Annex K survey method. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (proposed) |
| 2007-03 | [ISO 1996-2:2007](https://www.iso.org/standard/41860.html) | withdrawn | Annex C tonal audibility. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ISO 1996-2:2017 (Annex K survey method and Table J.1; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | not stated | — |
| [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) | Python | ISO 1996-2:2017 (Annex K prominent-tone detection) | — | not stated | Proposed (https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/52). Pull request from May 2022; no maintainer reply. |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ISO 1996-2:2007 (Annex C; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | not stated | — |

**See also:** [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html), [Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.html)

## References

1. ISO 1996-2:2007. Acoustics — Description, measurement and assessment of environmental noise — Part 2: Determination of environmental noise levels. https://www.iso.org/standard/41860.html
2. ISO 1996-2:2017. Acoustics — Description, measurement and assessment of environmental noise — Part 2: Determination of sound pressure levels. https://www.iso.org/standard/59766.html

# Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** IEC 61400-11, wind turbine tonality, tonal audibility

Tonality analysis in the acoustic noise measurement of wind turbines: tones are identified in narrow-band spectra and their tonal audibility is reported.

**In short.** The current edition is IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python).

# Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/impulsiveness.html

**Quantity:** Impulsiveness · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112, impulsiveness, impulse adjustment, impulsive sound prominence

Objective prominence of impulsive sounds and the corresponding adjustment of the equivalent level in environmental noise assessment: Nordtest method NT ACOU 112 and ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022 (adjustment of 0 to 9 dB). Hearing-model impulsiveness metrics are not standardised and no open implementation is listed.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; NT ACOU 112; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022-07 | [ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/77035.html) | current | Publicly available specification. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2002-05 | NT ACOU 112 | current | Nordic test method. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022 (in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | not stated | — |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | NT ACOU 112 (in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | not stated | — |

## References

1. Nordtest (2002). *NT ACOU 112: Acoustics — Prominence of impulsive sounds and for adjustment of LAeq*. Nordtest, Taastrup.
2. ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022. Acoustics — Description, measurement and assessment of environmental noise — Part 3: Objective method for the measurement of prominence of impulsive sounds and for adjustment of LAeq. https://www.iso.org/standard/77035.html

# Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html

**Quantity:** Psychoacoustic annoyance · **Unit:** dimensionless · **Also known as:** PA, psychoacoustic annoyance, Zwicker annoyance, Widmann annoyance, More annoyance, Di annoyance

Psychoacoustic annoyance (PA) combines percentile loudness N5 with sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength (Widmann 1992; Zwicker & Fastl 1999). More (2010) added tonality and Di et al. (2016) adapted the model for tonal noise. None of these is standardised; ISO/AWI 26573, registered in 2026, covers the assessment of annoyance through listening tests, including prediction models.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference models are Widmann (1992), Zwicker & Fastl (1999), More (2010), and Di et al. (2016). In development: ISO/AWI 26573. Open-source implementations of it: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; Di et al. (2016)), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; Di et al. (2016)), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; More (2010)), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; More (2010)), [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; Zwicker & Fastl (1999)), and [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; Widmann (1992); unreleased).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-04 | [ISO/AWI 26573](https://www.iso.org/standard/93922.html) | in development | Approved work item (stage 20.00) since 2026. | — |
| 2016 | [Di et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apacoust.2015.12.006) | published | Adapted for tonal noise. | [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 2010 | More (2010) | published | Adds tonality. | [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 1999 | Zwicker & Fastl (1999) | published | Book version of the model. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html), [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 1992 | Widmann (1992) | published | Original model. | [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (unreleased) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | Di et al. (2016) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Di2016` | another implementation | — |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | Di et al. (2016) (since v1.0) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Di2016`, `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Di2016_from_percentile` | not stated | No verification routine (README). |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | More (2010) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_More2010` | another implementation | — |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | More (2010) (since v1.0) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_More2010`, `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_More2010_from_percentile` | not stated | No verification routine (README). |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | Zwicker & Fastl (1999) (since 3.1.0) | `psychoacoustic_annoyance`, `psychoacoustic_annoyance_from_signal` | standard or paper data | Follows Eqs. 16.2–16.4 of Fastl & Zwicker (2007), the textbook form of Widmann's model. |
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | Zwicker & Fastl (1999) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Zwicker1999` | another implementation | — |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | Zwicker & Fastl (1999) (since v1.0) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Zwicker1999`, `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Zwicker1999_from_percentile` | not stated | — |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | Widmann (1992) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Widmann1992`, `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Widmann1992_from_percentile` | not stated | Unreleased. Added on `main` in June 2025; the README describes it as the same model as the Zwicker & Fastl entry under its original attribution. |

## References

1. Widmann, U. (1992). *Ein Modell der psychoakustischen Lästigkeit von Schallen und seine Anwendung in der Praxis der Lärmbeurteilung* [Doctoral dissertation, Technische Universität München].
2. Zwicker, E., & Fastl, H. (1999). *Psychoacoustics: Facts and models* (2nd ed.). Springer.
3. More, S. R. (2010). *Aircraft noise characteristics and metrics* [Doctoral dissertation, Purdue University]. PARTNER report PARTNER-COE-2011-004.
4. Di, G., Chen, X., Song, K., Zhou, B., & Pei, C. (2016). Improvement of Zwicker's psychoacoustic annoyance model aiming at tonal noises. *Applied Acoustics*, 105, 164–170. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apacoust.2015.12.006
5. ISO/AWI 26573. Acoustics — Procedures for assessment and prediction of noise-induced perceptual annoyance through laboratory-based listening tests. https://www.iso.org/standard/93922.html

# Equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html

**Quantity:** Related quantities · **Unit:** dB SPL, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 226, equal-loudness contours, phon curves, threshold of hearing

Normal equal-loudness-level contours for pure tones in free-field listening. ISO 226:2023 replaced ISO 226:2003; ECMA-418-2:2025 still refers to the 2003 edition.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO 226:2023. Open-source implementations of it: [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python). Implementations of earlier editions or related models: [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) (Python; ISO 226:2003).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023-03 | [ISO 226:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/83117.html) | current | Third edition. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |
| 2003-08 | [ISO 226:2003](https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html) | withdrawn | Second edition; withdrawn in 2023. | [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ISO 226:2023 (since 3.1.0) | `equal_loudness_contour`, `equal_loudness_contours`, `loudness_level`, `hearing_threshold` | standard or paper data | — |
| [MoSQITo](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html) | Python | ISO 226:2003 (since 0.3.5) | `equal_loudness_contours` | not stated | The docstring gives no edition; it is based on Jeff Tackett's MATLAB code for ISO 226:2003. |

## References

1. ISO 226:2003. Acoustics — Normal equal-loudness-level contours. https://www.iso.org/standard/34222.html
2. ISO 226:2023. Acoustics — Normal equal-loudness-level contours. https://www.iso.org/standard/83117.html

# Perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/epnl.html

**Quantity:** Related quantities · **Unit:** PNdB, EPNdB · **Also known as:** EPNL, EPNdB, PNL, PNLT, perceived noisiness, noy, aircraft noise certification

Effective perceived noise level for aircraft noise certification: perceived noisiness in noy, the tone-corrected perceived noise level (PNLT) and a duration correction. Defined in ICAO Annex 16, Volume I, and in the US regulation 14 CFR Part 36.

**In short.** The current edition is ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I and 14 CFR Part 36. Open-source implementations of it: [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) (Python; 14 CFR Part 36), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) (MATLAB; 14 CFR Part 36), and [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) (Python; ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I; PNL, PNLT and EPNL, in the `phonometry.aircraft` namespace).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2002-07 | [14 CFR Part 36](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-36) | current | US regulation (Appendices A and B). | [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html), [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) |
| 2017-07 | [ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I](https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise) | current; Amendment 15 was adopted on 2026-03-27 and applies from 2027-01-01 (new noise limits and supersonic aeroplanes); whether it changes the EPNL procedure itself has not been confirmed. | International standard for aircraft noise certification. | [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [pySQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html) | Python | 14 CFR Part 36 | `EPNL_FAR_Part36` | another implementation | — |
| [SQAT](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html) | MATLAB | 14 CFR Part 36 (since v1.1) | `EPNL_FAR_Part36`, `get_PNL`, `get_PNLT`, `get_Duration_Correction` | another implementation | The README says no reference implementation or test signals exist, so it was only cross-checked. Follows Amendment 36-26 (2005). |
| [phonometry](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html) | Python | ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I (PNL, PNLT and EPNL, in the `phonometry.aircraft` namespace) | — | standard or paper data | Tested with the EPNL example of ICAO Doc 9501 (Environmental Technical Manual). |

## References

1. ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I. Annex 16 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation — Environmental Protection — Volume I: Aircraft Noise. https://store.icao.int/en/annex-16-environmental-protection-volume-i-aircraft-noise
2. 14 CFR Part 36. Noise standards: aircraft type and airworthiness certification (Appendix A: EPNL). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-36

# Aural detectability of sounds in background noise

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/aural-detectability.html

**Quantity:** Related quantities · **Unit:** d′ (detectability index), dB · **Also known as:** detectability, d-prime, signal detection, aural detection, audibility of aircraft

How likely a listener is to detect a sound in background noise, from signal-to-noise ratios in auditory filters and signal-detection theory. Used for aircraft, drone and urban air mobility noise. Not standardised.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference model is Fidell et al. (1974). No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1974 | [Fidell et al. (1974)](https://doi.org/10.1177/001872087401600405) | published | Model paper. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

## References

1. Fidell, S., Pearsons, K. S., & Bennett, R. (1974). Prediction of aural detectability of noise signals. *Human Factors*, 16(4), 373–383. https://doi.org/10.1177/001872087401600405

# MetaSona

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html

C library with a typed Python interface and prebuilt wheels, written to make repeated psychoacoustic analysis fast. Covers Zwicker loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel–Weber roughness, Aures tonality and ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness, roughness and tonality.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona
- **Documentation:** https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/docs/python-api.md
- **Language:** Python, C
- **Kind:** Library
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-only AND Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND MIT — The combined distribution is GPL-3.0; MetaSona's own code keeps Apache-2.0 and the adapted SQAT, MoSQITo and PocketFFT parts keep their BSD-3-Clause, MIT or Apache-2.0 notices.
- **Package:** PyPI `metasona` (https://pypi.org/project/metasona/)
- **Install:** `pip install metasona`
- **Latest release:** 0.2.2 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-25 (active)
- **Maintainers:** Jiahua Zhang
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — README and NOTICE state that it was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels; since 0.1.0) | `stationary_loudness`, `time_varying_loudness`, `loudness_from_levels` | available | another implementation | Model tables taken from MoSQITo and checked element by element; one upper-slope value (0.22) follows the ISO 532-1 reference C table where MoSQITo uses 0.24. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo; since 0.2.0) | `loudness_ecma`, `ecma_tonal_analysis` | available | another implementation | Adapted from the SQAT/RefMap MATLAB code by Lotinga and Torjussen. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html) | DIN 45692:2009 (from specific loudness; since 0.1.0) | `sharpness_din45692` | available | not stated | — |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | Daniel & Weber (1997) (since 0.1.0) | `roughness_daniel_weber` | available | another implementation | Follows SQAT revision `e6228b78`, which includes SQAT's September 2026 rewrite. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied; since 0.2.0) | `roughness_ecma` | available | another implementation | Uses the standard's 20 ms grid and nominal calibration factor, where SQAT uses a slightly adjusted calibration. |
| [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html) | Aures (1985b) (since 0.1.0) | `tonality_aures` | available | another implementation | Follows SQAT's September 2026 revision (250 ms Hann windows, 125 ms hop); exact agreement with MATLAB is not established. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono or stereo; since 0.2.0) | `tonality_ecma`, `ecma_tonal_analysis` | available | another implementation | — |

## Notes

- First commit and first PyPI release on 2026-09-16.
- Ports a pinned SQAT revision (`e6228b78`, after SQAT's September 2026 fixes) and model data from MoSQITo; differences to both are listed in [THIRD_PARTY.md](https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY.md).
- Expects calibrated pressure in pascals. The Python interface resamples to 48 kHz; the C functions require 48 kHz.
- The README reports speed-ups over MoSQITo 1.2.1 (e.g. 73× for time-varying loudness on its benchmark signal).

## Before you rely on it

- The README calls the current version experimental, particularly roughness and tonality, and says standards conformance has not been established.
- Comparisons with SQAT and MoSQITo are described as kept outside the package repository, and the third-party notes say exact agreement with the MATLAB code is not established.

## Sources

- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY.md
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/NOTICE
- https://pypi.org/project/metasona/

# MoSQITo

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/mosqito.html

Python library for sound quality metrics: ISO 532-1 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness, ECMA-418-2 loudness and roughness (2nd edition), tone-to-noise and prominence ratios, and the speech intelligibility index. Widely used, but without a release or a commit since April 2024.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo
- **Documentation:** https://mosqito.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0
- **Package:** PyPI `mosqito` (https://pypi.org/project/mosqito/)
- **Install:** `pip install mosqito`
- **Latest release:** 1.2.1 (2024-04)
- **Last commit:** 2024-04-22 (inactive since 2024-04)
- **Maintainers:** Eomys / Green Forge Coop
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** San Millán-Castillo, R., Latorre-Iglesias, E., Glesser, M., Wanty, S., Jiménez-Caminero, D., & Álvarez-Jimeno, J. M. (2021). MOSQITO: an open-source and free toolbox for sound quality metrics in the industry and education. *INTER-NOISE 2021*, INCE Conference Proceedings 263(5). https://doi.org/10.3397/IN-2021-1767
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying; since 1.0.0) | `loudness_zwst`, `loudness_zwst_perseg`, `loudness_zwst_freq`, `loudness_zwtv` | available | standard or paper data | Validation scripts use the ISO 532-1 Annex B test signals; the documentation marks it as validated. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.) (since 1.2.0) | `loudness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data | Followed the 1st edition (2020) in versions 1.0.0–1.1.1 and the 2nd edition (2022) from 1.2.0. Validation scripts compare with figures of the standard. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html) | DIN 45692:2009 (weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl; since 1.0.2) | `sharpness_din_st`, `sharpness_din_tv`, `sharpness_din_perseg`, `sharpness_din_from_loudness`, `sharpness_din_freq` | available | standard or paper data | Validation scripts use the DIN 45692 test signals; the documentation marks it as validated. |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | Daniel & Weber (1997) (since 1.0.0) | `roughness_dw`, `roughness_dw_freq` | available | standard or paper data | The documentation marks it as validated against reference data. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.) (since 1.2.0) | `roughness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data | The documentation still lists it as under development. An open pull request (#95) fixes the low-pass filter range, which caused discrepancies with SQAT for time-varying signals. |
| [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html) | Aures (1985b) | — | proposed | not stated | Pull request from April 2026 following the improved Aures metric of Estreder et al. (2023); no maintainer reply. |
| [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html) | ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.) (since 1.0.2) | `tnr_ecma_st`, `tnr_ecma_perseg`, `tnr_ecma_freq`, `pr_ecma_st`, `pr_ecma_perseg`, `pr_ecma_freq` | available | not stated | Docstrings say "ECMA 418-1" without an edition; the helper code and the bibliography cite ECMA-74 Annex D (17th edition, 2019). The documentation marks it as available but not validated. |
| [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html) | ISO 1996-2:2017 (Annex K prominent-tone detection) | — | proposed | not stated | Pull request from May 2022; no maintainer reply. |
| [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) | ISO 226:2003 (since 0.3.5) | `equal_loudness_contours` | available | not stated | The docstring gives no edition; it is based on Jeff Tackett's MATLAB code for ISO 226:2003. |

## Notes

- Started by EOMYS in 2020. The default branch is `master`; its last commit and the last release (1.2.1) are both from 2024-04-22.
- The documentation lists Soundscapy as a user; several other projects (PsychoBox, Sonemeter and others) wrap it.
- Also computes the ANSI S3.5 speech intelligibility index (`sii_ansi`), which is outside the scope of this index.
- Open, unanswered pull requests add Aures tonality ([#97](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/97), 2026), ECMA-418-2 roughness fixes ([#95](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/95), 2026) and an ISO 1996-2 Annex K tone detector ([#52](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/52), 2022).
- A C#/.NET port, Mosqito.NET, was announced in issue [#98](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/issues/98) (not checked).

## Before you rely on it

- No maintainer has answered issues or pull requests opened since 2024, including bug reports on TNR/PR (#80,
- `import mosqito` fails when matplotlib is not installed, because it is imported but not declared as a dependency ([#100](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/issues/100)); install matplotlib yourself.
- Its ECMA-418-2 functions follow the 2nd edition (2022), two editions behind the current one.

## Sources

- https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/blob/master/README.md
- https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/blob/master/docs/source/user_guide/scope.rst
- https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/tree/master/validations
- https://pypi.org/project/mosqito/
- https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/issues/100
- https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/95
- https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/97

# phonometry

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/phonometry.html

Python acoustics library (formerly PyOctaveBand) that added a large psychoacoustics module in July 2026: ISO 532-1, -2 and -3 loudness, ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness, tonality, roughness and fluctuation strength (monaural), DIN 45692 sharpness, Osses fluctuation strength, ECMA-418-1:2024 TNR/PR, tonal audibility, impulsiveness, EPNL and ISO 226:2023. Only NumPy and SciPy are required.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry
- **Documentation:** https://jmrplens.github.io/phonometry/
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library
- **Licence:** MIT
- **Package:** PyPI `phonometry` (https://pypi.org/project/phonometry/)
- **Install:** `pip install phonometry`
- **Latest release:** 3.3.0 (2026-07)
- **Last commit:** 2026-10-01 (active)
- **Maintainers:** José M. Requena Plens
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — The draft paper (`paper/paper.md`) has an AI usage disclosure: language models drafted code, tests and documentation from the author's clause-by-clause readings, under the author's direction and review. 34 commits from July 2026 contain Claude Code session links.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary and time-varying; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_zwicker`, `loudness_zwicker_from_spectrum` | available | standard or paper data | Written from the Annex A reference program; Annex B test signals are used in the tests. |
| [Moore–Glasberg loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html) | ISO 532-2:2017 (with binaural inhibition; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_moore_glasberg`, `loudness_moore_glasberg_from_spectrum`, `loudness_moore_glasberg_from_third_octave` | available | standard or paper data | The documentation says it reproduces the Annex B tone and broadband cases to within a percent or two. |
| [Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html) | ISO 532-3:2023 (since 3.1.0) | `loudness_moore_glasberg_time` | available | standard or paper data | Documented deviations: it runs at the native sample rate instead of resampling to 32 kHz, and the Annex B WAV-file cases are not reproduced (Annex C values are used instead). |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono only; since 3.1.0) | `loudness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data | Checked at the calibration signal only, where it gives 0.9843 sone_HMS (−1.55 %). |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html) | DIN 45692:2009 (also the informative Aures and von Bismarck variants; since 3.1.0) | `sharpness_din`, `sharpness_din_from_specific` | available | standard or paper data | Checked with the DIN 45692 reference signal and Table A.2. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono only; no entropy weighting; since 3.1.0) | `roughness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data | Checked at the calibration signal only. |
| [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) | Osses et al. (2016) (since 3.1.0) | `fluctuation_strength` | available | standard or paper data | Compared with Table 1 of Osses et al. (2016) and with SQAT (correlation 0.98). Validated for amplitude modulation only; a steady 1 kHz tone reads about 0.09 vacil. |
| [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) | Fastl & Zwicker (2007) (closed-form expression for amplitude-modulated noise; since 3.1.0) | `fluctuation_strength_am_noise` | available | not stated | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono only; since 3.3.0) | `fluctuation_strength_ecma` | available | standard or paper data | Checked at the calibration signal only (0.993 vacil_HMS); misprints found in Clause 9 are listed in its errata. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono only; since 3.1.0) | `tonality_ecma` | available | standard or paper data | Checked at the calibration signal only. |
| [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html) | ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.) (since 3.1.0) | `tone_to_noise_ratio`, `prominence_ratio`, `assess_tones` | available | standard or paper data | The "prominent" flag applies the numeric criterion only. |
| [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html) | ISO/PAS 20065:2016 (since 3.1.0) | `tone_audibility`, `analyze_spectrum`, `audibility_from_levels`, `mean_audibility`, `audibility_uncertainty` | available | standard or paper data | Follows the 2016 PAS, not the 2022 TS. Does not apply the A-weighting required by clause 5.3.2. |
| [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html) | ISO 1996-2:2017 (Annex K survey method and Table J.1; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | available | not stated | — |
| [Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html) | ISO 1996-2:2007 (Annex C; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | available | not stated | — |
| [Tonal audibility of wind turbines (IEC 61400-11)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.html) | IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018 | `wind_turbine_tonality` | available | not stated | — |
| [Impulse prominence](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/impulsiveness.html) | ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022 (in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | available | not stated | — |
| [Impulse prominence](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/impulsiveness.html) | NT ACOU 112 (in the `phonometry.environment` namespace) | — | available | not stated | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | Zwicker & Fastl (1999) (since 3.1.0) | `psychoacoustic_annoyance`, `psychoacoustic_annoyance_from_signal` | available | standard or paper data | Follows Eqs. 16.2–16.4 of Fastl & Zwicker (2007), the textbook form of Widmann's model. |
| [Equal-loudness contours](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html) | ISO 226:2023 (since 3.1.0) | `equal_loudness_contour`, `equal_loudness_contours`, `loudness_level`, `hearing_threshold` | available | standard or paper data | — |
| [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/epnl.html) | ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I (PNL, PNLT and EPNL, in the `phonometry.aircraft` namespace) | — | available | standard or paper data | Tested with the EPNL example of ICAO Doc 9501 (Environmental Technical Manual). |

## Notes

- Renamed from PyOctaveBand (octave-band filtering) at 3.0.0 on 2026-07-06; the psychoacoustics module arrived in 3.1.0 on 2026-07-13. 873 of its 905 commits are from 2026.
- The README reports 1793 of 1793 conformance checks passing across 519 standards, generated by the project's own CI ([CONFORMANCE.md](https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/docs/CONFORMANCE.md)).
- Keeps a public errata list of misprints found in standards, including ECMA-418-1:2024 and ECMA-418-2:2025 ([ERRATA.md](https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/docs/ERRATA.md)).
- A JOSS-format paper draft exists in the repository; no published paper yet. Version 4.0 (release candidate since 2026-09-10) moves modules.
- {'Not implemented': 'Daniel & Weber roughness, Aures tonality, More and Di annoyance, and binaural combination for ECMA-418-2.'}

## Before you rely on it

- Single maintainer; all validation comes from the project's own tests.
- The ECMA-418-2 checks only use the calibration signals, and no comparison with another implementation is reported. Its loudness reads 0.984 sone_HMS at the calibration point, which its own documentation says is outside the adjustment the standard allows.
- Requires Python 3.13 or newer.

## Sources

- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/docs/CONFORMANCE.md
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/docs/ERRATA.md
- https://github.com/jmrplens/phonometry/blob/main/paper/paper.md
- https://jmrplens.github.io/phonometry/
- https://pypi.org/project/phonometry/

# pySQAT

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/pysqat.html

Python port of the MATLAB toolbox SQAT (README title "SQAT4PY") with a PySide6 graphical interface. Covers ISO 532-1 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber roughness, Osses fluctuation strength, Aures tonality, three psychoacoustic annoyance models and EPNL; its ECMA-418-2 functions call sottek-hearing-model.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library
- **Licence:** none — No licence file at the repository root. The bundled copy of SQAT v1.3 (MATLAB, used as the validation reference) carries SQAT's CC-BY-NC-4.0 licence.
- **Latest release:** no release
- **Last commit:** 2026-06-27 (active)
- **Maintainers:** Gerard Mendoza Ferrandis
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | ISO 532-1:2017 | `Loudness_ISO532_1` | available | another implementation | Compared with SQAT (MATLAB). |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) | `Loudness_ECMA418_2` | available | not stated | A wrapper that calls sottek-hearing-model. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html) | DIN 45692:2009 | `Sharpness_DIN45692`, `Sharpness_DIN45692_from_loudness` | available | another implementation | Compared with SQAT (MATLAB). |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | Daniel & Weber (1997) | `Roughness_Daniel1997` | available | another implementation | Compared with SQAT v1.3, before SQAT's September 2026 rewrite. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) | `Roughness_ECMA418_2` | available | not stated | A wrapper that calls sottek-hearing-model. |
| [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) | Osses et al. (2016) | `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016` | available | another implementation | — |
| [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html) | Aures (1985b) | `Tonality_Aures1985` | available | another implementation | A June 2026 commit corrected its calibration; it predates SQAT's September 2026 fixes. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) | `Tonality_ECMA418_2` | available | not stated | A wrapper that calls sottek-hearing-model. |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | Di et al. (2016) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Di2016` | available | another implementation | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | More (2010) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_More2010` | available | another implementation | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | Zwicker & Fastl (1999) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Zwicker1999` | available | another implementation | — |
| [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/epnl.html) | 14 CFR Part 36 | `EPNL_FAR_Part36` | available | another implementation | — |

## Notes

- Developed since May 2025 under the PALILA-TUDelft GitHub organisation; no release or tag yet.
- Validation scripts run SQAT in MATLAB and compare the Python results with it; the generated reports are not committed.

## Before you rely on it

- Without a licence, reuse rights are unclear, and the bundled MATLAB code is licensed for non-commercial use only.
- The ports follow SQAT v1.3 and do not include SQAT's 2026 fixes to ISO 532-1 time-varying loudness, Daniel & Weber roughness and Aures tonality.

## Sources

- https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT/tree/main/validation
- https://github.com/PALILA-TUDelft/pySQAT/issues/1

# sottek-hearing-model

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sottek-hearing-model.html

Python implementation of the ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th edition) Sottek Hearing Model metrics: loudness, tonality and roughness, with binaural combination, and fluctuation strength on the main branch. Translated from the MATLAB code used in SQAT and the RefMap project.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind:** Library
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-only — The LICENSE file has always been GPL-3.0 and the project metadata was changed to GPL-3.0-only on 2026-08-31; the metadata of the current PyPI release (0.1.14) still says AGPL-3.0-only.
- **Package:** PyPI `sottek-hearing-model` (https://pypi.org/project/sottek-hearing-model/)
- **Install:** `pip install sottek-hearing-model`
- **Latest release:** 0.1.14 (2026-03)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-18 (active)
- **Maintainers:** Mike Lotinga
- **AI assistance:** not stated
- **Paper:** Lotinga, M. J. B., Torjussen, M., & Felix Greco, G. (2025). Verified implementations of the Sottek psychoacoustic Hearing Model standardised sound quality metrics (ECMA-418-2 loudness, tonality and roughness). *Forum Acusticum / Euronoise 2025*, Málaga. https://doi.org/10.61782/fa.2025.0951
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (mono or stereo, with combined binaural output; since 0.1.9) | `shm_loudness_ecma`, `shm_loudness_ecma_from_comp` | available | standard or paper data | Unit tests check the standard's calibration signals (1 kHz, 40 dB gives 1 sone_HMS); the MATLAB code it was translated from was compared with commercial reference software in the paper. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (with combined binaural output; since 0.1.9) | `shm_roughness_ecma` | available | standard or paper data | — |
| [Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (needs at least 1.37 s of signal; binaural option) | `shm_fluctuation_ecma` | unreleased | another implementation | Merged on 2026-09-18. A draft report compares it with the MATLAB version (equal to floating-point precision) and with HEAD ArtemiS SUITE v17 (calibration 0.994 vs 1.003 vacil_HMS; recordings −8 % to +12 %). Five departures from the printed equations, judged to be misprints, are documented. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) (since 0.1.9) | `shm_tonality_ecma` | available | standard or paper data | Optional experimental tonal-annoyance weighting (Sottek & Becker, 2019) since 0.1.14. |

## Notes

- The paper verifies the MATLAB implementations of the 3rd edition, from which this package was translated; it does not cover the Python package itself.
- Maintained by one person at the University of Salford (RefMap project). Requires Python 3.11 or newer.
- pySQAT calls this package for its ECMA-418-2 metrics.

## Before you rely on it

- Fluctuation strength is only on the main branch (not on PyPI yet) and its verification report is marked as a draft.
- Versions up to 0.1.13 are affected by an empty-array bug fixed in 0.1.14 ([#9](https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/issues/9)).

## Sources

- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/blob/main/LICENSE
- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/blob/main/docs/validation/fluctuation_strength_verification.md
- https://pypi.org/project/sottek-hearing-model/
- https://github.com/mlotinga/sottek-hearing-model/issues/9

# SQAT

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/sqat.html

MATLAB toolbox for sound quality analysis that bundles most psychoacoustic metrics in one place: ISO 532-1 and ECMA-418-2 loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel & Weber and ECMA-418-2 roughness, Osses fluctuation strength, Aures and ECMA-418-2 tonality, four psychoacoustic annoyance models and EPNL. Each metric has its own verification routine.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT
- **Documentation:** https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT#readme
- **Language:** MATLAB
- **Kind:** Toolbox
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-or-later (main) / CC-BY-NC-4.0 (releases) — The default branch has been GPL-3.0-or-later since 2026-09-15, with BSD-3-Clause (ISO 532-1 loudness), MIT (Daniel & Weber roughness and nine utilities) and CC0-1.0 (colour maps) exceptions. Every release up to and including v1.3 is CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial) at repository level, while 21 metric files in v1.3 carry BSD-style notices and the ECMA-418-2 files say GPL-3.0.
- **Latest release:** v1.3 (2025-04)
- **Last commit:** 2026-10-02 (active)
- **Maintainers:** Gil Felix Greco, Roberto Merino-Martínez, Alejandro Osses, Mike Lotinga
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — Header comments in 20 files changed in August and September 2026 say the changes were assisted by Claude (Anthropic) and verified by the authors; 32 commits carry AI co-author trailers. The README has no AI statement.
- **Paper:** Felix Greco, G., Merino-Martínez, R., Osses, A., & Langer, S. C. (2023). SQAT: a MATLAB-based toolbox for quantitative sound quality analysis. *Proceedings of INTER-NOISE 2023*, Chiba, Japan. https://doi.org/10.3397/IN_2023_1075
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | ISO 532-1:2017 (stationary and time-varying; since v1.0) | `Loudness_ISO532_1`, `Loudness_ISO532_1_from_wavfile` | available | standard or paper data | Checked with the 25 test signals of Annex B.2–B.5 against the standard's tolerances. Fixes to the time-varying procedure are on `main` only (PR #48). |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) | `Loudness_ECMA418_2`, `LoudnessFromComp_ECMA418_2` | unreleased | another implementation | Updated to the 4th edition on `main` in 2025. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.) (mono or two channels with binaural combination; since v1.3) | `Loudness_ECMA418_2`, `LoudnessFromComp_ECMA418_2` | available | another implementation | Checked against equal-loudness contours and against reference results from commercial software on a binaural recording. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html) | DIN 45692:2009 (DIN 45692 weighting, plus von Bismarck and Aures options; since v1.0) | `Sharpness_DIN45692`, `Sharpness_DIN45692_from_loudness`, `Sharpness_DIN45692_from_wavfile` | available | standard or paper data | Checked with the narrowband and broadband test signals of DIN 45692. |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | Daniel & Weber (1997) (since v1.0) | `Roughness_Daniel1997`, `Roughness_Daniel1997_from_wavfile` | available | standard or paper data | Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature. Rewritten on `main` (PR #65, 2026-09-08) after revised code from Dik Hermes: 63 of 119 validation values go up and 56 down (largest change 0.155 asper). |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) | `Roughness_ECMA418_2` | unreleased | another implementation | Amended to the 4th edition on `main` in November 2025. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.) (with binaural combination; since v1.3) | `Roughness_ECMA418_2` | available | another implementation | — |
| [Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html) | Osses et al. (2016) (since v1.0) | `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016`, `FluctuationStrength_Osses2016_from_wavfile` | available | standard or paper data | Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) | `FluctuationStrength_ECMA418_2` | proposed | not stated | Open pull request since 2026-09-17. |
| [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html) | Aures (1985b) (since v1.0) | `Tonality_Aures1985`, `Tonality_Aures1985_from_wavfile` | available | standard or paper data | v1.3 is checked with one signal-to-noise comparison. Eight defects were fixed on `main` in September 2026 (for example, only one tonal component's level excess entered the result, and tones were removed from the wrong spectrum), with new checks against Aures's Figs. 5 and 6. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) | `Tonality_ECMA418_2` | unreleased | another implementation | A verification against Annex B.2 (PR #79) was merged and reverted on 2026-09-21 because the Annex B values of the 2025 edition appear to be out of date. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.) (since v1.3) | `Tonality_ECMA418_2` | available | another implementation | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | Di et al. (2016) (since v1.0) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Di2016`, `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Di2016_from_percentile` | available | not stated | No verification routine (README). |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | More (2010) (since v1.0) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_More2010`, `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_More2010_from_percentile` | available | not stated | No verification routine (README). |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | Zwicker & Fastl (1999) (since v1.0) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Zwicker1999`, `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Zwicker1999_from_percentile` | available | not stated | — |
| [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) | Widmann (1992) | `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Widmann1992`, `PsychoacousticAnnoyance_Widmann1992_from_percentile` | unreleased | not stated | Added on `main` in June 2025; the README describes it as the same model as the Zwicker & Fastl entry under its original attribution. |
| [Perceived noise level and EPNL](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/epnl.html) | 14 CFR Part 36 (since v1.1) | `EPNL_FAR_Part36`, `get_PNL`, `get_PNLT`, `get_Duration_Correction` | available | another implementation | The README says no reference implementation or test signals exist, so it was only cross-checked. Follows Amendment 36-26 (2005). |

## Notes

- The README lists 61 studies and theses that use SQAT. Software DOI (all versions) [10.5281/zenodo.7934709](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7934709).
- The latest release is v1.3 (2025-04-04); about 200 commits have been made on `main` since. Most of the metric-correctness work of August–September 2026 came from an external contributor through about 20 pull requests.
- The ECMA-418-2 functions come from the RefMap MATLAB code by Lotinga and Torjussen (University of Salford).
- Open pull requests: [#78](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/78) (ECMA-418-2 fluctuation strength) and [#84](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/84) (graphical interface).

## Before you rely on it

- The latest release (v1.3) is licensed for non-commercial use only; the GPL licence applies to the unreleased `main` branch.
- `main` contains breaking fixes that are not in any release: six deviations in ISO 532-1 time-varying loudness ([#48](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/48); test signal 10 deviated by 18.14 % in v1.3), eight defects in Aures tonality ([#67](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/issues/67)), a rewrite of Daniel & Weber roughness ([#65](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/65)), the sound level meter time weighting ([#51](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/51)) and a faster annoyance calculation ([#42](https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/42)). Results from v1.3 and `main` differ.
- The README warns that `main` may contain changes that are not yet fully verified and recommends using a release.

## Sources

- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/blob/main/LICENSE
- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/blob/main/citation.cff
- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/releases
- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/issues/67
- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/48
- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/65
- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/78
- https://github.com/ggrecow/SQAT/pull/79
